MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Sex: Female
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

SPECIMEN DETAILS
Specimen Type: Breast tissue, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Pathology Number: [redacted ID]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Clinical Diagnosis: Multifocal breast cancer
Reason for Testing: HER2 status evaluation for treatment planning

TEST PERFORMED
HER2 (ERBB2) Gene Amplification by Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed using FDA-approved dual-color probe for HER2/ERBB2 (17q12) and chromosome 17 centromere (CEP17). The PathVysion HER2 DNA Probe Kit was utilized according to manufacturer's specifications. A total of 80 interphase nuclei were analyzed from invasive tumor areas. Results were correlated with HER2 immunohistochemistry findings.

RESULTS

HER2/ERBB2 FISH Analysis:
- Mean HER2 copy number per cell: 1.84
- Mean chromosome 17 centromere copy number per cell: 1.81
- HER2/Chr17 ratio: 1.01
- Number of cells analyzed: 80

Interpretation: NEGATIVE for HER2 gene amplification

The HER2/Chr17 ratio of 1.01 is below the threshold of 2.0 for amplification. The mean HER2 copy number of 1.84 per cell is below the alternative criterion of ≥6.0 copies per cell. These findings are consistent with HER2 negative status by current ASCO/CAP guidelines.

NOTE: Tissue sections showed evidence of cut-through artifact. While no amplification was detected in the cells analyzed, tissue heterogeneity cannot be completely excluded.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This HER2 negative result indicates that the patient is not eligible for HER2-targeted therapies such as trastuzumab, pertuzumab, or T-DM1. Treatment planning should proceed according to HER2-negative breast cancer protocols.

REFERENCES
Wolff AC, et al. Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 Testing in Breast Cancer: American Society of Clinical Oncology/College of American Pathologists Clinical Practice Guideline Focused Update. J Clin Oncol. 2018;36(20):2105-2122.

Reported by: [redacted name], MD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
Report Date: [redacted date]
